paper.title: Two for One: Privileged Bilateral Learning for Monocular Retinal Disease Classification

inputs.data: toy simulated paired-eye features (not ODIR images)

tiles.label: AUROC, left eye only
tiles.sub: baseline → privileged student; Δ 95% CI [-0.033, +0.012] (1,000 bootstraps)

tiles.label: Robust across cohorts?
tiles.sub: independent cohorts/splits where AUROC improved; mean Δ +0.024 ± 0.021

figures.title: Does the one-eye student beat the one-eye baseline?
figures.caption: Left: test ROC curves; dots = operating point at the threshold that maximised macro-F1 on validation. Right: metrics with 95% bootstrap CIs (1,000 resamples of the test set).

figures.title: When does the privileged eye help?
figures.caption: Δ AUROC (student − baseline) as the two eyes' disease signals become more correlated, for different distillation weights α (mean of 2 simulated cohorts per cell). Extension, not in the paper.

figures.title: One split or many?
figures.caption: The paper reports a single split. Left: Δ AUROC over independent simulated cohorts and splits. Right: the precision/FPR change at the validation-chosen threshold flips direction between splits.

compare.paper: AMD left FPR 0.011 → 0.027, precision 0.760 → 0.595; DR left FPR 0.766 → 0.089, precision 0.078 → 0.760
compare.note: both directions happen; depends on the validation threshold
